why: The rule whose target is the WHOLE REPOSITORY (`write: "./"`), and the file that found gate-map hole 8 on this corpus's first run. `matchesPath` reduces `"./"` to the empty string and then refuses the empty string, so this rule answers false for every input. Nothing is mis-enforced — the rule is `auto`, the compiler refuses `auto` wholesale and gate.mjs reads only gated and prohibited — and the divergence is real. **Since 2026-09-03 the `gated`/`prohibited` half of that divergence is refused at compile time** (#337 option 3, `neverMatches` in cli/compile.mjs), so it can no longer be compiled — and so can no longer merge, `compile` and `doctor` both running inside the required `workspace-verify` check. Nothing fires at commit time: that tier is `auto`, and the hook, which does read this policy, acts only on gated and prohibited. This rule is `auto`, the tier is refused one step earlier, and its target still answers false for every input — so every case below still expects FALSE and this file is unchanged in substance. What `./` should MEAN as a policy target is still open, and closing the hazard did not answer it. Every case below therefore expects FALSE and says which fact it is pinning.
